subject: Materials Science
title: Concrete: The Original Composite
description: A fast breakdown of Concrete: The Original Composite for builders.

hook.text: Reinforced concrete is a composite — cement paste matrix with steel bar reinforcement.

buildup.text: Concrete resists compression brilliantly but cracks instantly under tension.

discovery.text: Steel rebar handles the tension that concrete can't — a complementary composite partnership.

twist.text: Concrete and steel expand at nearly the same rate with heat — a lucky coincidence that makes them compatible.

climax.text: Every skyscraper, bridge, and dam on Earth relies on this concrete-steel composite.

punchline.text: The world's most-used composite is stone glued around steel.

quiz.question: Why do concrete and steel work well together?
options: They have similar thermal expansion and complement each other's weaknesses
Steel prevents concrete from getting wet
